title: Air-sea formation of sigma0 26.4-26.6 gives the sign of 10 of 11 North Atlantic AOU changes on 26.5 (1988-2021) at 1.6 times their size; North Pacific transformation across 26.5 fell 90%
abstract: Question: earlier campaign work found that a tracer-calibrated outcrop model gives the sign of North Atlantic (NA) AOU changes on sigma0 26.5 but makes the 1997-2012 changes 5-20 times too small, while the NA outcrop kept its area. Is the missing process the air-sea formation rate of the 26.4-26.6 class? Approach: Walin water-mass transformation from ERA5 monthly fluxes (1979-2022; NCEP R1 and R2 as checks), OISST/ERSSTv5 SST and WOA23 decadal surface salinity, and a one-box renewal model with an oxygen-use rate (4.6 umol/kg/yr) and renewal time from tracers and mean AOU, not fitted to the changes. The plan was written first. Results: NA formation was weak in 1998-2003 (0.8 Sv), strong in 2004-2011 (6.7 Sv) and weak in 2013-2021 (1.9 Sv). It predicts the thickness of the 26.5 class at BATS (r 0.56, surrogate p 0.008; passed in 15 of 16 runs). The model gives the sign of 10 of 11 GLODAP line-pair AOU changes (r 0.87); the slope of observed on model change is 0.62 (0.36-0.88), so the model is about 1.6 times too large and the pre-registered size test failed (the outcrop model had slope 3.4). Formation alone does not give the long-term BATS rise (ratio -0.19 to 0.35; failed). Exploratory: outcrop and formation models are both needed on the pairs (r 0.89), and their sum without a fit gives +11.8 against +11.9 umol/kg at BATS (1989-1998 to 2016-2025). In the North Pacific (NP), the air-sea transformation across 26.5 fell from 2.0 to 0.2 Sv (1984-1996 to 2009-2022; NCEP 2.1 to 0.1), as band area fell 40% and flux per area fell 75%; the NA stayed at 12-14 Sv. The NP box-model test passed with ERA5 but failed with NCEP R1 and R2, where the NP class has no net air-sea formation. Interpretation: NA AOU swings on 26.5 follow how much water winter buoyancy loss converts into the class; outcrop geometry gives the slower trend. Limitations: air-sea formation ignores mixing and is not subduction; monthly means; decadal salinity; one-box model; ERA5 ends 2022; exploratory parts added after the tests.
